name: Heat Exchanger Calculator (LMTD Method)
description: Calculate heat transfer rate using the LMTD (Log Mean Temperature Difference) method: Q = U × A × LMTD.

seo.title: Heat Exchanger Calculator - LMTD Method
seo.description: Heat exchanger calculations — Q = U × A × LMTD for thermal design and sizing

formula.expression: u * area * ((t1_hot - t2_cold) - (t2_hot - t1_cold)) / log((t1_hot - t2_cold) / (t2_hot - t1_cold)) / 1000
formula.explanation: Q = U × A × LMTD where LMTD = (ΔT1 − ΔT2) / ln(ΔT1/ΔT2). Counter-current flow assumed. ΔT1 = T_hot_in − T_cold_out, ΔT2 = T_hot_out − T_cold_in.

content.introduction: Calculate heat transfer rate for a heat exchanger using the Log Mean Temperature Difference (LMTD) method. This calculator assumes counter-current flow and uses the standard Q = U·A·LMTD formula.

example.description: 50m² exchanger, U=500 W/m²K, ΔT1=50°C (hot in−cold out), ΔT2=40°C (hot out−cold in), LMTD=44.8 → Q ≈ 1120 kW

faq.a: Log Mean Temperature Difference accounts for the varying temperature driving force along the heat exchanger. It is the logarithmic average of the temperature differences at each end.

faq.q: What is a typical U value?
faq.a: For liquid-liquid exchangers: 300-1000 W/m²K. For gas-liquid: 50-300 W/m²K. For condensing/boiling: 1000-5000 W/m²K.

faq.q: How do I convert heat duty between kW and MMBtu/hr?
faq.a: 1 kW = 3412 BTU/hr = 0.003412 MMBtu/hr. For example, 100 kW = 0.3412 MMBtu/hr. Convert to consistent units for exchanger sizing.

faq.q: What is the difference between counter-current and co-current flow?
faq.a: In counter-current flow the hot and cold streams enter at opposite ends, giving the largest LMTD and the smallest area for a given duty. In co-current (parallel) flow both enter at the same end; the temperature approach is limited and LMTD is lower, so more area is needed. The formula in this calculator assumes counter-current flow, which is the usual design choice for shell-and-tube exchangers.

sections.heading: Unit Conversion for Heat Exchanger Duty
sections.body:
**Heat duty units**

- 1 kW = 3412 BTU/hr = 0.003412 MMBtu/hr
- 1 MMBtu/hr = 293.1 kW
- 1 W = 3.412 BTU/hr

**Temperature units**

- °F = °C × 9/5 + 32
- ΔT in °C = ΔT in K

**Area units**

- 1 m² = 10.764 ft²

Exchanger duty Q = m × cp × ΔT or Q = U × A × LMTD. Keep mass flow, specific heat, and temperature difference in one consistent unit system before computing.

sections.heading: Worked Example: LMTD Step by Step
sections.body:
Size the duty of a shell-and-tube exchanger with hot fluid 100 C in, 60 C out, and cold fluid 20 C in, 50 C out (counter-current), U = 500 W/m2K, area = 50 m2.

Step 1 - temperature differences at each end: Delta-T1 = T_hot_in - T_cold_out = 100 - 50 = 50 K. Delta-T2 = T_hot_out - T_cold_in = 60 - 20 = 40 K.

Step 2 - LMTD = (50 - 40) / ln(50/40) = 10 / 0.2231 = 44.8 K.

Step 3 - duty Q = U x A x LMTD = 500 x 50 x 44.8 = 1,120,000 W = 1120 kW.

Check the unit conversion section to express this as BTU/hr (1120 kW = 3.82 MMBtu/hr).

sections.heading: Typical Overall Heat Transfer Coefficients
sections.body:
Selecting a realistic U value is the most uncertain part of an LMTD design. Typical ranges:

| Service | U (W/m2K) |
|---|---|
| Water to water | 800 - 1500 |
| Water to oil | 100 - 350 |
| Steam to water | 1000 - 4000 |
| Steam to oil | 100 - 300 |
| Gas to gas | 10 - 60 |
| Gas to water | 30 - 100 |
| Condensing refrigerant to water | 400 - 1000 |

Use the low end of the range when fouling is expected or the service is dirty; the design U must include an allowance for fouling (typical 0.0002 - 0.0006 m2K/W fouling resistance). Verify the U against manufacturer data or Perry's Handbook for the final design.
